message.content:
The three most significant schisms in Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Approximate Date | Key Parties | Main Issue(s) |
|---|--------|------------------|-------------|---------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East‑West Schism)** | 1054 CE | Eastern Orthodox Church vs. Roman Catholic Church | Doctrinal differences (e.g., Filioque clause, papal primacy), cultural and political tensions |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 CE | Various European reformers (Luther, Calvin, Anglicans, etc.) vs. Roman Catholic Church | Authority of Scripture vs. tradition, indulgences, church hierarchy, doctrinal disputes |
| 3 | **East‑West Schism (Second Great Schism)** | 1965 CE | Eastern Orthodox Church vs. Roman Catholic Church (re‑affirmation of the 1054 split) | Modern reaffirmation of the 1054 division, with renewed emphasis on theological and ecclesiastical differences |

These three events are often cited as the pivotal moments that reshaped the structure, theology, and political landscape of Christianity across the centuries.
